title: Spanakopita Spiral
subtitle: Spinach and feta filo coiled into a round tin
excerpt: A single coiled roll of filo, spinach, and feta baked in a round tin. The spiral gives each slice a mix of crisp outer layers and a soft, savoury centre.
sourceNotes: Greek spanakopita tradition. The spiral shape is a practical home-cook format that reduces offcuts and bakes evenly.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked. Cook from frozen at 180C for 50 to 55 minutes. Do not freeze once baked as the filo turns soft.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble and refrigerate unbaked for up to a day. Bake straight from the fridge.

content.text: This spiral version of spanakopita is more forgiving than individual triangles. The whole roll coils into a round tin, so no complex folding is needed. Squeeze the spinach as dry as you can or the filling will make the filo soggy.
Wilt the spinach in a dry frying pan over a high heat, in batches if needed. Once cool enough to handle, squeeze out as much water as possible in your hands. Roughly chop and place in a large bowl.
Add the feta, beaten eggs, spring onion, dill, nutmeg, and black pepper to the bowl. Mix well. Taste and add salt only if needed since feta is already salty.

Heat the oven to 190C. Brush a 23cm round tin with melted butter. Lay one sheet of filo on a clean work surface with the long edge facing you. Brush all over with butter. Place a second sheet on top and brush again.
Spoon a line of filling along the long bottom edge, leaving a 2cm border. Roll the filo up tightly away from you into a long log.

Coil the log in the centre of the tin. Continue making logs with the remaining filo and filling, coiling each one around the last to fill the tin. Brush the top generously with the remaining melted butter.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden and crisp on top. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting. The layers will hold together once they settle.

items.cause: The spinach was not squeezed dry enough before mixing.
items.fix: Squeeze the wilted spinach in a clean tea towel, twisting hard, until almost no water comes out.

items.cause: The filo dried out while working.
items.fix: Cover unused sheets with a damp tea towel and work quickly. Small tears are fine; they close up when rolled.

items.symptom: The filling leaks out at the edges.
items.cause: Too much filling was placed close to the edges.
items.fix: Leave a clear 2cm border along the bottom and sides before rolling each log.
